cases.question: Current AX-17 renal guidance in Germany?
cases.answer:
For AX-17 in Germany, the renal dose modification guidance is as follows:

*   **Normal renal function** (eGFR >=90): Starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, with routine monitoring [E2].
*   **Mild renal impairment** (eGFR 60-89): Starting dose is 50 mg OD, maximum is 100 mg/day, with routine monitoring [E2].
*   **Moderate renal impairment** (eGFR 30-59): The approved German renal starting dose is 25 mg once daily [E1, E3]. The maximum dose is 50 mg/day, and monitoring requires recheck 2-4 weeks [E2].
*   **Severe renal impairment** (eGFR 15-29): Requires specialist review, with a maximum dose of 25 mg/day, and enhanced monitoring [E2].

cases.question: Compare AE evidence in HN-204 and HN-311.
cases.answer:
In HN-204, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 12.7%, Headache 14.0%, Fatigue 15.3%, Dizziness 16.6%, Rash 17.8%, and Transaminase elevation 19.1% [E1]. For the control group in HN-204, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E1]. Transaminase elevation was a serious adverse event in HN-204 [E1]. The highest treatment % in HN-204 was transaminase elevation (19.1%) [E4].

In HN-311, treatment-emergent adverse events for AX-17 were: Nausea 11.8%, Headache 13.0%, Fatigue 14.2%, Dizziness 15.4%, Rash 16.6%, and Transaminase elevation 17.7% [E2]. For the control group in HN-311, these were: Nausea 6.0%, Headache 6.6%, Fatigue 7.2%, Dizziness 7.8%, Rash 8.4%, and Transaminase elevation 9.0% [E2]. Transaminase elevation was a serious adverse event in HN-311 [E2]. The highest treatment % in HN-311 was transaminase elevation (17.7%) [E4].

Comparing HN-311 to HN-204, the treatment % for AX-17 was lower in HN-311 for all listed adverse events: Nausea was -0.9 points lower (11.8% vs 12.7%), Headache was -1.0 points lower (13.0% vs 14.0%), Fatigue was -1.1 points lower (14.2% vs 15.3%), Dizziness was -1.2 points lower (15.4% vs 16.6%), Rash was -1.2 points lower (16.6% vs 17.8%), and Transaminase elevation was -1.4 points lower (17.7% vs 19.1%) [E4, E1, E2]. All treatment % differences (HN-311 minus HN-204) lie between -1.4 and -0.9 points [E4]. The control group percentages for all listed adverse events were identical between HN-311 and HN-204 [E4, E1, E2].

Sources
[E1] HN-204 · HN-204 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2025-06-12 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-204_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E2] HN-311 · HN-311 Clinical Study v1.0 · APPROVED · effective 2026-01-18 · p.11, Table 14
     https://storage.cloud.google.com/tredence-fde-1-medevidence-vks/raw/HN-311_Clinical_Study.pdf#page=11
[E4] computed by code from [E3] (differences and highest values; not document text)

Descriptive comparison across separate studies, not a head-to-head result.

cases.question: My 70-year-old patient in Germany has eGFR 35 and ALT 4x ULN. Should I give him 50 mg?
cases.answer:
Individual treatment decisions are for the treating physician. I've routed your question to Medical Information (escalation ESC-8419654D); they will follow up.

General reference from the controlled documents (not a recommendation for an individual patient):
For patients with moderate renal impairment (eGFR 30-59), the approved German renal starting dose for AX-17 is 25 mg once daily, with a maximum dose of 50 mg/day [E2, E1]. Monitoring for this category requires rechecking in 2-4 weeks [E2].

Renal dose modification by eGFR category is as follows:
*   **Normal** (eGFR >=90): Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Monitoring Routine [E2].
*   **Mild** (eGFR 60-89): Starting dose 50 mg OD, Maximum 100 mg/day, Monitoring Routine [E2].
*   **Moderate** (eGFR 30-59): Starting dose 25 mg OD, Maximum 50 mg/day, Monitoring Recheck 2-4 weeks [E2].
*   **Severe** (eGFR 15-29): Specialist review, Maximum 25 mg/day, Monitoring Enhanced [E2].

Regarding hepatic monitoring, baseline hepatic laboratory values are required, with repeat testing between Day 14 and Day 21 [E1].
